title: Roasted Tomato & Basil Soup
summary: A make-ahead starter that tastes better the next day, once the flavours have melded. Light and acidic, it will not sit heavily before a rich main course.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to {temp:200}. Put the tomatoes cut-side up on a large baking tray and add the onions, red pepper and whole garlic bulb.
Drizzle with the olive oil and balsamic vinegar, and sprinkle with the sugar, salt and pepper.
Roast for {timer:40-45}, until the tomatoes have collapsed and the edges are caramelised.
Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves out of their skins into a bowl.
Transfer everything to a large pan and add the stock and most of the basil.
Simmer for {timer:10}, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream, if using, and reheat gently before serving.
Garnish with fresh basil and a drizzle of olive oil, and serve with crusty bread.

tips: Roasting concentrates the tomato flavour and adds a smoky sweetness. Make it 1–2 days ahead; the flavour deepens. Reheat gently, and do not let it boil once the cream is in.
